prompt: Please generate an image. Locked painterly style: hand-painted stylized game art, chunky readable shapes, detail painted not modelled, mid-level detail, softer muted colours with gentle saturation, epic and luminous, never grim. The palette's warm gold and cool teal are painted into the surfaces, but the light is flat, even studio light: no strong key light, no cast shadows, no rim light. Use the attached images only as reference as described: the first attachment is always the style reference for palette and brushwork; later attachments are the approved designs to keep. Game-asset reference sheet for 3D modelling, wide landscape 16:9. Plain light neutral grey background, no scene, no sky, no clouds, no floating rock, no ground plane, a soft contact shadow only. Every piece fully isolated with clear space around it, nothing overlapping, nothing touching the edge, arranged in tidy rows, each with a small neat hand-lettered label underneath. SPECIES sheet for a creature built from a shared body-plan kit: BURROW BOAR, a stocky wild boar with russet bristles, short curved tusks and a mossy patch on its back, pawing the turf, built on the four-legged body plan; about 0.8 m at the shoulder. Storm-touched variant "Stormtusk": Hostile. Its charge leaves a trail of crackling static that slows anyone who crosses it. Keep the base body and parts from the attached kit sheets and the creature's design from the attached plate. Show the assembled creature in side view and three-quarter view at the centre; around it, each part it uses pulled out with a thin leader line to its socket and a small label naming the part. Below: a row of four square colour mask swatches (main, secondary, accent, pattern). If the creature has a storm-touched variant, show it small at the right in side view, labelled. A plain neutral 1.8 m human silhouette labelled "1.8 m" stands on the sheet for scale, with everything at true scale to it. Place it beside the side view, at TRUE scale to the stated size. Title at the top: "Burrow Boar".
